How to log Wildlife sightings

There are three ways to log your sightings of each animal in GTA 6. The first is for any creature that is close to you. You can focus by holding L2/LT, then press and hold R1/RB to study that animal. Once you fill the circle, that creature will be logged in your wildlife sighting progression track, which you can look at by opening the sub-menu.

If you'd rather not get up close and personal with an alligator, or if you're trying to track the many bird species in Leonida, you can equip the binoculars from your weapon wheel. You can zoom in using the D-Pad, but you'll need to track that animal as you use the Study prompt. This is certainly easier said than done, particularly for small or fast birds, but you'll eventually get the hang of it.

Finally, for any fishing-related animal sightings, you need to catch them with a fishing rod. One of the early missions in Chapter 1 teaches you everything you need to know about catching fish. Essentially, you cast out the line, reel it back in slowly to tempt a fish to bite, then, once you have one on the hook, you tire it out by pulling on the line in the opposite direction. Once you're holding it, it will be added to your log.

If you want to catch the bigger fish in the area, you'll need more lures, which are sold at some Ammu-Nations. Use the map to browse through the stores that sell lures. Not every one will have a full inventory, so make sure you get the type you need for the waters you're fishing in.

  • Mammals - 18 species
  • Cats & Dogs - 34 species
  • Reptiles & Amphibians - 6 species
  • Birds - 60 species

  • Other - 23 species

title: All Meditation Spots In GTA 6
summary:
Sometimes, you just want to step away and relax from all the hustle and bustle in Grand Theft Auto 6. By “hustle,” we mean ransacking the vaults of banks, and by “bustle,” we mean running over hundreds of people with trucks. So, why not head to the wilderness in search of Meditation Spots? You might even find inner peace while you’re at it.

In This Article
  • How Meditation Spots work in Grand Theft Auto 6
    • Meditation Spots in Mariana County
      • Meditation Spot #1: Intro to Meditation
      • Meditation Spot #2: Smooth Sand Meditation
    • Meditation Spots in Kelly County
      • Meditation Spot #3: Swamp Meditation
      • Meditation Spot #4: Worn Stone Meditation
      • Meditation Spot #5: Red Rocks Meditation

How Meditation Spots work in Grand Theft Auto 6

Meditation Spots are a type of activity that you can do when you’re not tackling missions. You simply need to go to specific areas, sit down, and then press the corresponding button prompts to complete breathing exercises.

As an aside, even if Jason and Lucia are together during a run, they have to do their meditation exercises separately. Try to be patient since each process can take a while.

Meditation Spots in Mariana County

There are a couple of GTA 6 Meditation Spots in Mariana County. They’re on opposite ends of the zone and one of them is technically missable.

Meditation Spot #1: Intro to Meditation

This Meditation Spot is actually the porch/deck of Jason’s house in Key Lento. To unlock it, play through chapter 1 normally until Lucia notices that Jason seems stressed out. She’ll eventually encourage him to meditate on the porch, so follow her to start the tutorial.

Take note that this sequence is missable if you leave the house instead of listening to Lucia’s prompt. Be sure to finish this task prior to undertaking the important job/mission that you receive from Mattia.

Meditation Spot #2: Smooth Sand Meditation

You’ll find this Meditation Spot in the northern tip of Belpoint, an island west of Capri. The point-of-interest consists of neatly arranged stones on a sandbar.

Meditation Spots in Kelly County

You’ll head to Kelly County for the campaign’s second chapter. The Meditation Spots in the zone are actually far from areas that you tend to go to for missions, so be ready for a bit of a trek.

Meditation Spot #3: Swamp Meditation

Found in the swamplands in the southeastern part of Kelly County. You visit this area if you’re doing Moses’ mission to find a BF Bandito.

Meditation Spot #4: Worn Stone Meditation

This GTA 6 Meditation Spot is at the back of the dirt path in Camp Moonflower, which counts as a WAiNK Curiosity. It’s behind a parked hippie van.

Meditation Spot #5: Red Rocks Meditation

To reach this area, travel along Moonstone Highway leading northeast out of Port Gellhorn. You should see the map label for Manifest Canyon and, once you’re past that, look for a sloping path up the hill.

You’re going to feel lost as you explore the cities, beachfronts, and seedy underbelly of Leonida. If you need more help navigating the massive game world and tackling its activities, be sure to check our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

title: How To Play Tennis And All Court Locations In GTA 6
summary:
Tennis was one of the most beloved minigames from Grand Theft Auto 5, and by all indications, it appeared that Rockstar Games was bringing it back for GTA 6. However, players are dozens of hours into the game by this point, and the tennis minigame has still eluded everyone.

While there are plenty of golf courses and racing challenges for players to participate in, no tennis icon appears in GTA 6. However, there are several fully fleshed-out tennis courts spread across Leonida, so what exactly is going on with the tennis minigame?

In This Article
  • Can you play tennis in GTA 6?
  • All tennis court locations in GTA 6
    • Courtland Park Stadium
    • Port Vice City
    • Ocean Beach
    • Washington Beach
    • Rialto Islands (Catalan Island)

Can you play tennis in GTA 6?

Technically, tennis is a playable minigame in GTA 6. However, it's not nearly as complete as the other minigames, such as golf, billiards, and racing.

Instead, tennis looks to be in a similar spot to the basketball minigame. You can freely pick up rackets and tennis balls in GTA 6, but no location offers you the ability to play against NPCs or other characters in full-on matches. You're only able to hit the ball with the racket, and this doesn't even have to be on a tennis court.

Compared to GTA 5, which lets you play hour-long matches against Michael's wife or other characters, this is quite the step down when it comes to tennis. However, Rockstar Games has said certain minigames simply couldn't be implemented in time, and it looks like they prioritized other content over tennis in GTA 6.

Still, with minigames like tennis and basketball included in GTA 6, future updates or even DLC could expand on them. After all, there are plenty of tennis courts to make use of in Leonida.

All tennis court locations in GTA 6

There are several tennis courts you can find and enter in GTA 6. It's at these courts where you'll be able to find a tennis racket and ball to pick up and practice your serves with. However, no matter how long you stand around, no opponent will show up to offer you a match.

Still, whether you want to see the courts or maybe remember them for the future, you can see every tennis court location in GTA 6 below.

Courtland Park Stadium

This is the largest and most recognizable tennis court in GTA 6. Located in the center of Catalan Key in Vice-Dale County, this is a massive tennis stadium that also has a few separate tennis courts surrounding it. If tennis ever comes to GTA 6 as a full minigame, this is likely where it will start.

Port Vice City

Strangely enough, there's a random tennis court in the center of Port Vice City. There seems to be no reason for it to be there, but you've likely driven by it several times without even realizing.

Ocean Beach

With a neighborhood as wealthy as Ocean Beach, you have to expect at least one tennis court. This one is located right outside of a large building across the street from Lucciano's poolside bar and restaurant.

Washington Beach

Washington Beach is another rich neighborhood that features a tennis court. You can find this court right near the Y Hotel beach in the central part of Washington Beach.

Rialto Islands (Catalan Island)

The final tennis court we were able to find in GTA 6 is located in the Rialto Islands. Specifically, on the western side of Catalan Island, you can find a couple of courts nestled in the backyard of some wealthy homeowners.

For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

That's a pretty sharp departure from the rest of the games in the series, where you could use them from the start of a fresh save, but it does lean into forcing your first playthrough to be as realistic as possible--something that Rockstar has strived for with GTA 6.   • Unlock: Finish the story.
  • $250,000 cheat code: Up, Right, Down, Left, Up, Left, Down, Right.

title: Alan Wake Dev’s Forgotten TV-Action Game Hybrid Is At A Huge Discount Right Now
summary:
I loved Quantum Break. In fact, I dare say that I still love it to this day. Combining Remedy’s pizzazz for third-person shooters with the boldness to add TV show elements to the narrative experience, Quantum Break’s time-bending power fantasy is one that hooked me from start to finish. After playing it at launch, I let the dust settle before playing it once again in the early 2020s, and now, it’s time for another playthrough—and you may as well join me when it’s this cheap.

After Alan Wake’s horror-led approach, with Stephen King vibes oozing from the entire experience, I don’t think any of us expected it to become a larger part of a connected universe. Quantum Break may not officially be part of the same universe, but it feels like the foundation of what would eventually become Remedy’s connected universe.

You play as Jack Joyce, who, after catching up with his time-machine-making friend Paul Serene, is interrupted by Jack’s brother, Will, who says using it will cause time to end. Of course, if that happened, the game wouldn’t continue. Instead, both Jack and Paul are afflicted by chronon radiation, giving the pair time-related abilities. Soldiers appear, causing a ruckus on the university campus, led by an older, more dangerous Paul. Gasp!

It’s no surprise that a narrative focusing on time-travel shenanigans offers, well, time-travel shenanigans. But between missions, you’ll get to see real actors playing the characters in a series-style format, which gives you a nice break between some incredibly fun missions. That’s right, Remedy’s continued prowess in third-person shooter action is still here, and the time abilities give you some truly fun ways to deal with enemies.

You can send out bubbles that freeze enemies in place, fire a barrage of bullets into them, and watch them die a horrible death by countless simultaneous bullets. A dash lets you close the gap between Jack and any enemies giving you trouble from a distance, while a blast lets you levitate Monarch’s helpless soldiers into the air, making them vulnerable to your attacks. You can see Remedy’s vision for future games coming into play here—between Alan Wake 2’s heavy embrace of live-action moments and Control’s suite of powers, those games owe a lot to Quantum Break.

If you’re looking to give it a try, and I suggest you do, you can grab Quantum Break for just $8.40 / £6.30 at Fanatical. As a Remedy fan, it’s a truly exciting game to play through because you can see the developer’s vision years before Control and Alan Wake 2’s success. But as a general player, it’s a solid third-person shooter that blends a variety of genres to create something cinematic.

title: I Was Wrong About GTA 6
summary:
Some months ago, I wrote about how, even prior to its full reveal, we already knew what GTA 6 was going to be. Although not unique to the franchise by any means, GTA games had always followed a very clear formula, rarely upending it in any meaningful way. I strongly suspected that the 13-year wait for GTA 6 would result in a very pretty version of a very familiar game. As release approached, I worried that for all of the praise heaped upon its story and incredible level of detail, all of that was merely a veneer on the same game we've been playing for 25 years.

And in many ways, that is true; at its most basic level, GTA 6 is still a game about driving from point A to point B, and maybe shooting some ne'er-do-wells when you get there. But I dramatically underestimated the impact of that veneer, and just how differently a familiar formula can feel when accompanied by impactful systems and relationships.

The freeform nature of GTA 6's world, and the objectives you have over the course of a given mission, are largely identical to previous games. You can just drive around and make your own fun, or deal with violent drug smugglers, or pilot a boat or plane or car through a series of checkpoints. It's all very familiar on paper.

But never before in a GTA game have I considered whether I have time to go and do one of those things because I have someone I care about waiting at home. Only rarely in a GTA have I decided to drive carefully, lest I face the consequences of doing almost anything I'd traditionally associate with a GTA game.

So much of GTA 6's focus is on the relationship between Lucia and Jason. I quickly found myself caring about them both, and for all of Rockstar's talk of their romantic relationship being optional, I truly can't fathom playing this in a way that doesn't fully embrace their love. And the way that permeates things even in Chapter 1--the phone calls, the text messages, the interactions at home--has forced some degree of role-playing on me. 

I check the time on my in-game phone not because I'm wondering if it's late enough to meet a contact in the woods, but because I want to be sure I'm home in time to hang out, whether that's talking, watching TV, or browsing our respective phones together. Despite the insistence of your boss, Brian, that you get down to a meeting spot for your next mission, I delayed doing so because it was a long drive late in the day, and the thought of leaving my partner hanging was unacceptable.

Were that the only thing I was doing differently in GTA 6 than in past games, I think it would still fall into the category of veneer--a bit of narrative-laced framing that surrounds the usual chaos of going out and driving down sidewalks and blowing up cars. 

Instead, that more thoughtful approach to things extends to almost all of the moment-to-moment gameplay. I regularly drive the speed limit (something made much easier by the fantastic usage of the PS5's DualSense triggers). I tend to stay on the road and in my lane, and well away from any pedestrians or other cars. I do frequently blow through red lights, but only after looking both ways. When I pull off a robbery, I tend to target other criminals, rather than stores. I routinely pull over when I need to use my phone while driving. I don't hijack random cars driving by--some 25 hours in, I've not done this most basic of actions in a GTA game even once. 

A small amount of this does stem from that urge to role-play as these characters. Jason and Lucia might be criminals, but they also feel like real people, and it's hard to imagine them running over innocent bystanders or smashing up their cars because you're intent on reaching your destination in as little time as possible. Additionally, the fact that you have ownership of your vehicle--which can suffer damage and require repairs, needs gas, and stores weapons and drugs you've stolen--makes it feel far less like the disposable vehicles of the past (including the character-specific vehicles of GTA 5). By placing more emphasis overall on money and making you carefully consider how it gets spent, I'm less willing to suffer a dent to my ride or risk attracting police attention. 

The importance of your car also comes in part from both the increased difficulty of stealing any random vehicle you come across, the added value of your car (where you can reliably store things in the trunk), and the challenges of dealing with the police when you get a Wanted level. There's a sense of danger here that I've never felt before in a GTA game. Again, the role-playing factors here, as I don't want to "die" (such as you can), nor do I want to lose money, letting down my partner. I want to see them achieve their goals, but I also want to make the time I spend earning money mean something.

Furthermore, the realistic nature of the world, both in terms of the visual fidelity and the many fine details contained within, make it harder to treat NPCs as chaff. In GTA 6, I'd feel bad if I ran over a person--or, heaven forbid, a dog or cat--rather than feeling they are collateral damage I forget about 10 seconds later. Even hostiles, like the random criminals who attempt to hijack your car, I deal with as delicately as possible, which is to say, I shoot them in the leg; my body count in this game would regularly be eclipsed by five minutes of random gameplay in a past GTA game. 

Although I wouldn't have realized it before playing, this is what I wanted a GTA game to be at this point in my life. I'm less interested in the random chaos that made me fall in love with GTA 2 and 3 back in the day; instead, I want strong characterization, a story that I feel invested in, and gameplay systems that both reward and encourage thoughtful play. I no longer want to be an undeniable force that everything in Leonida revolves around; I want to exist as another believable aspect of this world.

This is not to say I won't ever go wild when I get my hands on a tank and wreak some havoc. But unlike in the past, doing so will be only a temporary distraction, not the main attraction. For that to be the case, and for me to be happy about it, is GTA 6's most remarkable accomplishment.

title: The Best Xbox Series X Games In 2026
summary:
These are the very best Xbox Series X|S games. The Xbox Series X|S has been around since 2020, and it's built a huge library of great games. With so much to choose from, we've curated a selection of the very best Xbox Series X|S games to play right now. We regularly review these choices to ensure we stand by them as the best the Xbox Series X|S has to offer, so this still stands as our highest recommendation for the console. As 2026 continues, this should serve as a starting point for finding the absolute cream of the crop.

The future of Xbox is a more expansive brand than just a console, encompassing its suite of services like Xbox Game Pass. The subscription service has emerged as a major pillar for Microsoft, offering a vast rotating library of free games, including first-party releases. Whether you're looking for something new to play via the Game Pass subscription service or need buying advice for your next full game purchase, this list of games will steer you in the right direction.

Most, but not all, of the games we've chosen are available on Xbox Game Pass. While the Series X boasts the best performance and visuals, the Series S also offers noticeable improvements and upscales to 4K. And lots can also be played on your Xbox One, either with Smart Delivery to optimize the experience or through Microsoft's cloud-streaming tech for games that outpace the last generation.

If you'd rather catch up with some older, but still excellent games, be sure to read our picks for the best Xbox One games, or upgrade your gaming gear with our picks for the best Xbox controllers and best Xbox headsets. And while you're at it, check out our best PS5 games, best PS4 games, and best Nintendo Switch games too.

007 First Light

IO Interactive being handed the keys to the James Bond franchise is what you'd call a match made in heaven. The studio has established itself as a powerhouse in open-world design and immersive gameplay, but with 007 First Light, IO proves that it knows how to tell a damn good story as well. Fusing its talent for creating intricate, elegantly designed levels with rock-solid fisticuffs and shooting gameplay, 007 First Light isn't just a fantastic James Bond game; it's the definitive origin story for the secret agent that we've been waiting decades for.

Read our 007 First Light Review.

Advertisement

Alan Wake 2

Remedy's Alan Wake is a cult classic of the survival horror genre, and since then the studio has been building its own universe with story ties to other releases like Control. Alan Wake 2 is the sequel 13 years in the making, and it delivers. The story follows the author Alan Wake and FBI agent Saga Anderson through a mind-bending dual campaign. It leans more into horror than its predecessor and contains some truly unforgettable moments.

Read our Alan Wake 2 review.

Arc Raiders

One of the biggest hits of 2025, Arc Raiders isn't just a well-designed extraction shooter. It's also a game where the community has come together to craft stories and moments you won't find anywhere else. The threat of being sniped by an opportunistic player is always present, but more often than not, you'll find yourself engaged in missions and events that make for perfect chatter around the office cooler. It's those constant surprises, unseen betrayals, and scrappy adventuring in a NASA-punk world that have helped propel Arc Raiders into the spotlight.

Read our Arc Raiders review.

Advertisement

The Blood of Dawnwalker

Games that impose a time limit on you can be a hard sell, but in The Blood of Dawnwalker, developer Rebel Wolves has cleverly managed to ease that tension by selectively moving the clock forward only when it truly matters. Rich worldbuilding, a grim medieval atmosphere, and multi-layered side quests also make this a standout game. With time moving forward whenever you take specific narrative or exploratory actions, there's a sense of urgency that propels you forward while you also grapple with the consequences of your actions.

Read our The Blood of Dawnwalker review.

Advertisement

Blue Prince

Blue Prince is an incredible puzzle adventure game that is bound to stay with you for a long time. As the inheritor of the stately Mount Holly manor, you are tasked with reaching the mysterious Room 46 in order to keep your new property. But this is no ordinary mansion, as the layout of rooms shifts every day. Each time you open a door you determine which room will be "drafted" on the other side, letting you create your own pathway. But as you learn more about the house, and how the rooms and their systems interact, you'll learn there's much more to Mount Holly than meets the eye.

Read our Blue Prince review.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4

After a few lackluster entries, Call of Duty feels better than ever with a full package that offers a cinematic single-player campaign, robust multiplayer, and an extraction shooter experience that will leave you sweating. The rebooted sub-series ends on a high note, pairing a tense, global military conflict with deep, character-driven storytelling; and while multiplayer is as solid as ever, we have a feeling the revamped DMZ mode will have a healthy player base for quite some time. Call of Duty established itself as the premier blockbuster series in the 2000s, and two decades later, it's still managing to strike a well-crafted balance between gritty realism and high-stakes online action.

Read our Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 review.

Castlevania: Belmont's Curse

Castelvania had been missing in action for years before The Rogue Prince of Persia developer Evil Empire resurrected, masterfully restoring the franchise to its metroidvania roots and adding in a few original ideas of its own. That mix of nostalgic gameplay, slick visuals, and an innovative Tarot card skill system raises the bar for the franchise, as Belmont's Curse captures Castlevania's iconic legacy with rewarding exploration and polished combat.

Read our Castlevania Belmont's Curse review.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33

There's a lot to love about Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, from its exquisite art direction through to its elegant marriage of turn-based RPG and souls-like influences, but one of the factors that makes it so mesmerizing is that it's consistently satisfying to play. Whether you're pumping your fist in delight after you execute a perfect series of parries or you're reeling from the emotional rollercoaster of its story, Expedition 33 will keep your eyes glued to it whenever you boot it up to continue your journey across its beautiful world.

Read our Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 review.

Control Resonant

Control Resonant could have easily been a retread of the linear corridor shootouts of its predecessor, but Remedy Entertainment took a big swing to create an ambitious, ability-driven action-RPG. That sense of freedom in exploring a version of Manhattan that has been turned upside down by a Hiss invasion is a big draw on its own, but the fast-paced melee combat and delightfully weird vibes seal the deal on one of Remedy's best games yet.

Denshattack

Few games are as capable of putting you in the zone--or making you scooch forward on your couch--like Denshattack is. It's a high-energy rollercoaster that turns an on-rails experience into an extreme sports spectacle as you master its fluid gameplay, sweaty palms and all. More than that, it's a throwback to classic Dreamcast and PS2-era titles like Jet Set Radio and Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater, and each stage wastes no time in introducing new mechanics and hazards for you to brave along the way. Paired with a vibrant visual style and one of the best soundtracks of the year, it's no wonder that Denshattack is an instant classic.

Doom: The Dark Ages

event_model_payload.headline: The Best Xbox Series X Games In 2026
event_model_payload.summary:
These are the very best Xbox Series X|S games. The Xbox Series X|S has been around since 2020, and it's built a huge library of great games. With so much to choose from, we've curated a selection of the very best Xbox Series X|S games to play right now. We regularly review these choices to ensure we stand by them as the best the Xbox Series X|S has to offer, so this still stands as our highest recommendation for the console. As 2026 continues, this should serve as a starting point for finding the absolute cream of the crop.

The future of Xbox is a more expansive brand than just a console, encompassing its suite of services like Xbox Game Pass. The subscription service has emerged as a major pillar for Microsoft, offering a vast rotating library of free games, including first-party releases. Whether you're looking for something new to play via the Game Pass subscription service or need buying advice for your next full game purchase, this list of games will steer you in the right direction.

Most, but not all, of the games we've chosen are available on Xbox Game Pass. While the Series X boasts the best performance and visuals, the Series S also offers noticeable improvements and upscales to 4K. And lots can also be played on your Xbox One, either with Smart Delivery to optimize the experience or through Microsoft's cloud-streaming tech for games that outpace the last generation.

If you'd rather catch up with some older, but still excellent games, be sure to read our picks for the best Xbox One games, or upgrade your gaming gear with our picks for the best Xbox controllers and best Xbox headsets. And while you're at it, check out our best PS5 games, best PS4 games, and best Nintendo Switch games too.

007 First Light

IO Interactive being handed the keys to the James Bond franchise is what you'd call a match made in heaven. The studio has established itself as a powerhouse in open-world design and immersive gameplay, but with 007 First Light, IO proves that it knows how to tell a damn good story as well. Fusing its talent for creating intricate, elegantly designed levels with rock-solid fisticuffs and shooting gameplay, 007 First Light isn't just a fantastic James Bond game; it's the definitive origin story for the secret agent that we've been waiting decades for.

title: How To Get A Helicopter In GTA 6
summary:
You’ll spend so many hours driving across the state of Leonida in Grand Theft Auto 6, that your feet will start to ache in the real world. But there are still other modes of travel that you can try out. And, yes, you can take to the skies as well on board a helicopter.

Helicopter spawns in Grand Theft Auto 6

As of the time of this writing, there’s no clear way to permanently own a helicopter in GTA 6. These vehicles can neither be saved near your safehouse, nor can they be delivered to wherever you are.

That said, there are several areas where helicopters frequently spawn. For the most part, you should look at helipad markings on the map--i.e. “H” symbol on rooftops and facilities. We’ve got a few examples below.

Early-game option: Buckingham Maverick

The Buckingham Maverick is a great early-game pick if you just want to explore and reveal more of the map. To find it, simply travel along the main highway from Jason’s home and keep going southwest until you reach Southwind. To the right, you’ll see MHH Marque Hoppers, which has a Maverick conveniently parked on the pier.

Military helicopters in GTA 6

While you’re in the area, you might be interested in getting a military helicopter in GTA 6. There are several options like the machine-gunning Buzzard, sleek Valkyrie, and beefy Cargobob. All of these are in the Mile Zero Base just a short distance away from Southwind.

You must be careful, though, because this is a military base that’s on high alert. If you get spotted within its boundaries, you’ll be warned by police and soldiers. Dawdle for too long and you’ll be reported for committing a crime, earning an instant 4-star Wanted Level for good measure. Having countless troops, including those in armored vehicles, shooting at you is not a good way to start the day.

Amphibious helicopters

It’s also a good idea to find amphibious helicopters like the Nagasaki Sea Sparrow. One is near the speedway in the southwestern part of Hamlet, and the other is further west at the halfway point between the town and Watson Bay. (It’s also where you obtain the Dominator Buggy if you own the Ultimate Edition.)

As the term implies, these types of choppers can take off/land on water, making them integral for thorough exploration of the seas surrounding Leonida.

Rooftop helipads in Vice City

There are many helicopters flying all over Vice City, and you can grab one of them by searching for the helipad icons on your map. Buildings with helipads on the roof tend to have interiors that you can enter, as well as elevators that can take you to the top floor. From there, you just need to hijack the vehicle and zip away to safety.

These are just some of the GTA 6 helicopters that you can acquire. Keep returning to these locations if you want them to respawn. As for other vehicles that you can steal, don’t forget to check our articles about tanks, planes, and boats.

You’re going to feel lost as you explore the cities, beachfronts, and seedy underbelly of Leonida. If you need more help navigating the massive game world and tackling its activities, be sure to check our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

Helicopter spawns in Grand Theft Auto 6

As of the time of this writing, there’s no clear way to permanently own a helicopter in GTA 6. These vehicles can neither be saved near your safehouse, nor can they be delivered to wherever you are.

That said, there are several areas where helicopters frequently spawn. For the most part, you should look at helipad markings on the map--i.e. “H” symbol on rooftops and facilities. We’ve got a few examples below.

Early-game option: Buckingham Maverick

The Buckingham Maverick is a great early-game pick if you just want to explore and reveal more of the map. To find it, simply travel along the main highway from Jason’s home and keep going southwest until you reach Southwind. To the right, you’ll see MHH Marque Hoppers, which has a Maverick conveniently parked on the pier.

Military helicopters in GTA 6

While you’re in the area, you might be interested in getting a military helicopter in GTA 6. There are several options like the machine-gunning Buzzard, sleek Valkyrie, and beefy Cargobob. All of these are in the Mile Zero Base just a short distance away from Southwind.

You must be careful, though, because this is a military base that’s on high alert. If you get spotted within its boundaries, you’ll be warned by police and soldiers. Dawdle for too long and you’ll be reported for committing a crime, earning an instant 4-star Wanted Level for good measure. Having countless troops, including those in armored vehicles, shooting at you is not a good way to start the day.

Amphibious helicopters

It’s also a good idea to find amphibious helicopters like the Nagasaki Sea Sparrow. One is near the speedway in the southwestern part of Hamlet, and the other is further west at the halfway point between the town and Watson Bay. (It’s also where you obtain the Dominator Buggy if you own the Ultimate Edition.)

As the term implies, these types of choppers can take off/land on water, making them integral for thorough exploration of the seas surrounding Leonida.

Rooftop helipads in Vice City

There are many helicopters flying all over Vice City, and you can grab one of them by searching for the helipad icons on your map. Buildings with helipads on the roof tend to have interiors that you can enter, as well as elevators that can take you to the top floor. From there, you just need to hijack the vehicle and zip away to safety.

These are just some of the GTA 6 helicopters that you can acquire. Keep returning to these locations if you want them to respawn. As for other vehicles that you can steal, don’t forget to check our articles about tanks, planes, and boats.

title: How To Steal And Register Cars With Advanced Trackers In GTA 6
summary:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has a massive world, and you can be sure that there are thousands of vehicles driving across the countryside at any given point in time. While the vast majority can be hijacked without worries--well, aside from cops that might see you--a select few have anti-theft devices that make them an unbearable hassle. Thankfully, there are ways to steal vehicles with Advanced Trackers.

Advanced Trackers: How exactly do they work?

The Advanced Trackers in GTA 6 can be seen if you scan most high-end vehicles like sports cars and luxury cars. Basically, if it looks expensive and sells for a high price, you can bet that it has an Advanced Tracker. Here’s how the device works:

  • Stolen vehicles with a Standard Tracker ping their location only if (a) they’ve significantly slowed down or stopped, and (b) a police car is nearby.
  • Advanced Trackers, meanwhile, ping their location if you go below a certain speed. You essentially need to put your pedal to the metal when driving them. Otherwise, the police would know your exact location.

Given the risk, most fence NPCs in the game won’t even accept stolen vehicles with Advanced Trackers. Well, except for one fella: Randy.

The legit method: Do missions for Randy

Randy is the one NPC in the game that accepts stolen cars with Advanced Trackers, but there are some caveats:

  • You meet Randy while tackling main missions in chapter 3. He’ll give you a task to steal a Zorrusso, which also nets you the Key Cloner, a tool that allows you to hijack keyless cars.
  • At this point, Randy and various Pay ‘n’ Spray shops will start accepting stolen vehicles with Standard Trackers.
  • He’ll also tell you that he has a “wishlist” of sorts: A dozen or so high-end cars that you need to boost and bring to his garage.
  • Note that some targets do have Advanced Trackers. He’ll only accept these as long as they’re part of his wishlist. Since he’ll keep them, you won’t be able to own/register them at all.
  • Again, you need to drive fast to prevent the tracker from triggering. But you also have to be careful since the sell value of the car will decrease depending on the damage.

Now, let’s say you’ve completed all of Randy’s requests. Come chapter 4, Randy will give you one more mission. This time, you need to boost a Mamba GT.

After that ordeal, you’ll be able to remove Advanced Trackers via Pay ‘n’ Spray shops in Leonida. Yes, you’ll finally be able to register/own all those high-end vehicles you keep seeing in Vice City.

The exploit method: Have your partner drive it

There’s also another method if you wish to steal cars with Advanced Trackers in GTA 6. It’s an exploit that involves fiddling around with partner controls. Here’s how to do it:

  • Have your partner tag along while you’re exploring.
  • Locate a car with an Advanced Tracker. Don’t do anything with it yet.
  • Look for a car near it, one that only has a Standard Tracker or no tracker at all. Make sure you unlock that vehicle.
  • Next, unlock the door of the car with the Advanced Tracker… and immediately exit it.
  • Open the partner interface by holding L2/LT. Then, select “You Drive.” This will cause your partner to enter the last vehicle that you interacted with--i.e. the one with the Advanced Tracker.
  • As for your own character, simply hop on to the other car that you jacked. Then, open the partner interface again and select “Follow.” (If your partner is driving the vehicle, they won’t trigger the tracker’s system.)
  • Drive your lowly vehicle to Randy’s shop, and watch as your partner follows behind you at a leisurely pace.
  • When you’re in front of Randy’s garage, simply switch to your partner and deliver the vehicle.

That’s it. No police chases, no need to drive over the speed limit, and no panicking due to the tracker’s alarm potentially going off.

title: All GTA 6 Book Swap Locations
summary:
Those who grew up in the 80s and 90s would remember things known as gamebooks, the precursors to modern-day role-playing and narrative-driven games. You might recall the Choose Your Own Adventure series and R.L. Stine’s Give Yourself Goosebumps, which presented you with choices, making you turn page after page to see the outcome.

Further back, we had classics like the Sorcery series and The Warlock of Firetop Mountain--co-written by authors Steve Jackson and Ian Livingstone, who coincidentally also founded Games Workshop (yes, the very company that owns Warhammer). Grand Theft Auto 6 pays homage to these works in the form of book swap locations, which you can find all over Leonida.

Book Swap collectibles in Grand Theft Auto 6

The book swaps in GTA 6 can be found in public bookcases outside homes--i.e. akin to little free libraries. Once you spot one, interact with it to browse the book’s contents. Yes, they function similarly to magazines and comics in that you can read a few excerpts. However, they’re part of a separate tally in the Collections page.

The literary works have silly dilemmas and humorous outcomes. It’s not quite interactive as, say, Tenebrae Lux on the JoyStation, but it’s still a nice nod that fans of gamebooks would appreciate.

Book Swaps in Mariana County

Book Swap #1

  • Pick Your Path: Horror - Killer Prom
  • Location: Inside a turtle-shaped container in the northeastern end of Dolphin Drive.

Book Swap #2

  • Pick Your Path: Fantasy - The Wizard’s Ruin
  • Location: Found in Beaumont Avenue in Watson Bay. It’s inside a blue bookcase in front of a white house.

Book Swap #3

  • Pick Your Path: Western - Badland’s Revenge
  • Location: This Book Swap in GTA 6 is in the wealthy neighborhood of Capri in the northwestern part of Mariana County. Go to Viola Street and look for the Halloween House, which also happens to be a WAiNK Curiosity.

Book Swaps in Vice-Dale County

Book Swap #4

  • Pick Your Path: Romance - Thighlander
  • Location: Found on SW 3rd Avenue in Southside.

Book Swap #5

  • Pick Your Path: Mystery - Goodnight, Dollface, Goodnight
  • Location: Go to Neptune Circle on Vespucci Island, which is in the northern part of the lake in Vice City.

Book Swaps in Leonard County and Kelly County

Book Swap #6

  • Pick Your Path: Survival - Outback Gas Junkie
  • Location: Head to Mamey Circle in the subdivision south of Waning Sands. Look for a large mushroom bookcase in the driveway. Oh, and be sure to open the garage door so you can grab a Liberty City Swingers collectible card.

Book Swap #7

  • Pick Your Path: Sci-Fi - Humanity Versus Space
  • Location: Drive to Reservoir Street, which is across the river northeast of Ambrosia.
